### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bd0469384343b5041c4f19080e2df24ce4442013` — the merge of head `1a99d2ae11d6931dbbc68e9c87f39d9e2d93cfee` into base `895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bd0469384343b5041c4f19080e2df24ce4442013 && git checkout bd0469384343b5041c4f19080e2df24ce4442013
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 1a99d2ae11d6931dbbc68e9c87f39d9e2d93cfee && git checkout -B drift-repro 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 && git merge --no-ff 1a99d2ae11d6931dbbc68e9c87f39d9e2d93cfee

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `1a99d2ae11d6931dbbc68e9c87f39d9e2d93cfee`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T14:36Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `895783a1` (5 files, +247/−9, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5 (area S3 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM

**What holds**

- Area point 1, the boot report:
  - `grantRefusal` asks `resolveCatalogReference` in the same scope as `catalogResolver`, `storedPermissionSetScope(column)`, which is the scope the authorization resolver reads. So the refusal it lists is the one the grant meets. It is asked only after the existing not-resolved and outside-namespace branches, and it is memoised per (name, column).
  - A catalog fault still stops the report (`ReportStop`) instead of being read as "no refusal".
  - A name nothing holds carries no `refusal`, and its line is byte-identical (CONTROL pin).
  - Each fix sentence is appended only when a refusal of its column class is listed, and both are true of the doors. `os migrate stored-references bind --table sys_user_permission_set …` exists, covers grants (R1), and writes only a still-null column. A grant that names its package is kept as written by the stamp seam (#32164), so "grant again naming its package, then remove" is a real path.
- Area point 2, H2 falsified, accepted. The bind text for a stale column was built in `resolveSuggestedSet` for a suggestion. `scope.packageId` there comes only from `permission_set_package`, because `storedPermissionSetScope` puts the suggesting package in `callerPackageId`, never in `packageId`. So a null column with a `package_id` correctly keeps the bind.
- The suggestion text names only doors that exist. "Install or enable that package again" is a package act. "Dismiss the suggestion" is `dismissAudienceBindingSuggestion`, which records the "no" on a pending row and revokes an acceptance on a confirmed one. So the withheld reason of an accepted row (pinned) also names a working door. Nothing tells the reader to edit the read-only table.
- Area point 3: the code, the `409`/`SuggestionStateError`, and every grant's effect are unchanged, so `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. The changeset is a patch.
- Ablations accepted: each of the three goes red on the pin it targets. The CONTROL keeps the "no refusal ⇒ neither fix" boundary.
- Area point 4: I agree with A (text only, no new door to clear a stale suggestion column) while nothing measures a need. The `os doctor` gap is correctly left out as a cli loose end.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

1. The appended fix sentences sit on one combined log line across organizations. That is fine for an operator, and the `refusals` meta lists each grant with its column, so nothing is ambiguous.

**Gates:** not judged. At review time 18 check-runs were in progress, 14 success, 16 skipped, none red. Land once all are green.
